summary: Point Escuminac's 1841 wooden light gave way to a concrete tower in 1965-66. Keepers, a 1901 fog-horn dispute and the 1959 Escuminac fishing disaster fill its record.

structures.note: Demolished in November 1966 (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett). Lighthouse Friends does not give a height.
Built 1965 per the register; 1966 per Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett. Coast Guard list: structure 22.4 m. Register: 18 m tall. Lighthouse Friends: 73 ft tall.

access.note: Coast Guard property. Grounds open; tower closed to visitors. Dirt road 4.6 km past Route 117 then 5 km of dirt; high-clearance vehicle advised by 2017 (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Petition from Miramichi merchants; House grants money for the light
Put into operation 12 August 1841; tenth lighthouse in the colony, first on its northern coast
Great easterly storm: thirty feet of shoreline lost in a few hours
Storm surge rose to the level of the ground floor of the dwelling and lighthouse
Third-order French Fresnel lens and new lantern, $1,301
Fog whistle in operation 1 June 1874 ($4,871)
Foghorn replaced the fog whistle
Schooner Levinia complaint over the fog horn; keeper's logbook exonerated him (Lighthouse Friends only)
Old fog-alarm building converted to an engine room; three-inch diaphone plant, $4,600
Life-saving station established at Escuminac
55 mm Diamond vapour installation replaces the duplex lamp
Escuminac life-boat crew rescued two men from the fishing smack Cormier in a gale, 16 November (year inferred from the fiscal-year report)
Schooner Minnie F. Crosby stranded on Escuminac reef; cargo salved and landed at Chatham (date not given)
St. John schooner struck the ground off the light; surveyed at Chatham, 2 June 1914
Electric lighting plant installed
Escuminac disaster, night of 19-20 June 1959: 35 fishermen died in a storm
Plans to demolish the 1841 lighthouse; Department reply on lens and lantern
Concrete hexagonal tower (register gives 1965)
Octagonal 1841 tower demolished in November 1966
De-staffed
Recognized Federal Heritage Building, register no. 21057

corrections.proposed: standing tower: hexagonal concrete, built 1965-66, 22.4 m; the 1841 octagonal wooden tower was demolished in 1966
corrections.why: The standing tower is the 1965-66 concrete tower. The 1841 wooden tower was demolished in 1966 (Lighthouse Friends, Rowlett). The record's 22.4 m matches the Coast Guard list for the concrete tower, so the build date is the error.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record lists the 1841 tower and the standing concrete tower as one structure. The 1841 octagonal wooden tower was demolished in 1966 and the concrete tower replaced it.

notes_for_editor: CHARACTERISTIC: the Coast Guard list (No. 1163) gives Fl W 3s, 22.0 m, 13 nm, matching the record. Rowlett describes three white flashes every 20 s and focal plane 20.5 m. Not resolved; the Coast Guard list is the one used. TOWER DATE: the register gives 1965; Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett give 1966; the story gives 1965 or 1966. HEIGHT: register 18 m; Rowlett 18 m (60 ft in the 1966 entry); Lighthouse Friends 73 ft; Coast Guard structure 22.4 m. ROCK: Lighthouse Friends sandstone, register shale; both stated in the story. LENS: the 1869 third-order French Fresnel lens belonged to the 1841 tower; Lighthouse Friends' 1965 note says the lens was to go to another station; its later location is not in the sources. Not put in facts. KEEPERS: the 1841-1873 keepers and the 1892-1939 McLennan dates are Lighthouse Friends only; the 1904 keepers' table places McLennan at Escuminac (OCR row, scan p. 172, printed page not read). The 1914 'H. L. Ascah'-style column matching does not apply here. LEVINIA 1901: Lighthouse Friends only; no matching name in the marine corpus (OCR may miss it). CORMIER: the report gives 16 November with no year; 1912 is inferred from the fiscal-year volume. MINNIE F. CROSBY: the report gives no date of stranding. ST. JOHN SCHOONER (1914): the OCR reads the name as '7. L. Colwell', not used in the story. DISASTER COUNTS: Lighthouse Friends says 54 boats set out and 22 sank; the Labour History site says 35 died. A YouTube item says 32 boats; not used. The monument is in the village at Escuminac Wharf, not at the light. LIVING PEOPLE: Kenneth Bliss McLennan, Merrill William Trenholm and P. Durell are named only as Lighthouse Friends lists them. Survivors of the 1959 disaster are not named. NOT READ: the federal Directory of Federal Heritage Designations page (the fetch returned no register text; the Heritage Guide copy was used). Chronicling America was not searched (Canadian station). Journal of the House of Assembly for 1820 and 1840 was not checked. CHECKED 2026-10-27: the whole Lighthouse Friends page was read (1820 address, 1840 petition, 1846 road, 1869 lens, 1874 whistle, 1887 foghorn, 1892 dismissals, 1901 Levinia, 1906-07 diaphone, 1959 disaster, 1965-66 demolition and tower all match the story). The 1904 keepers' table row was checked on the page image (1905 volume, printed p. 159, scan p. 172): McLennan, Kenneth | Escuminac Light and Fog Alarm | Mar. 7, 1892 | 750.00. Lighthouse Friends gives $700 for 1892; the 750 figure is not in the OCR text, so the story gives only the LF figure and does not footnote the table's salary; the disagreement is for the editor. The story's 'coxswain' role for E. F. Fleiger was removed: the 1909 life-saving table row (OCR, scan 221) gives his name and station, not a role. 'Three-inch' is Lighthouse Friends' wording; the report corpus does not show it. Minnie F. Crosby cargo (OCR, scan 336): 197 puncheons partly filled with molasses and 184 barrels of sugar. The Coast Guard list height (22.0) is given as 'a height' because the list's height reference was not read.
